# Remote Work Policy for International Contractors

Effective March 1, 2026. This policy applies to independent contractors who work with Acme Digital from outside Argentina and invoice for their services. Employees follow the hybrid work policy instead. Owners: Finance (Carolina Benítez, CFO) and People & Culture (Florencia Ibarra). Questions about this policy go to contractors@acme.example.

## Invoicing

- Invoice once a month for the services of the previous calendar month.
- Send your invoice between the 1st and the 3rd business day of the month.
- All invoices must be issued in US dollars (USD); we cannot accept invoices in local currency.
- Address the invoice to Acme Digital S.R.L. and include your tax ID, the hours worked per client and your bank details.
- Email the PDF to invoices@acme.example with the subject line "Invoice – Full Name – MM/YYYY", and attach the hours report your lead approved in Notion.
- Invoices that arrive after the 3rd business day are paid in the following month's cycle.

## Payment terms

- Approved invoices are paid on the 15th of each month. If the 15th is not a business day in Argentina, payment goes out on the next business day.
- Payments are sent by international wire transfer from our account at Woodgrove Bank.
- Acme covers the sending bank's fee; intermediary and receiving bank fees are paid by the contractor.
- If an invoice has an error, Finance tells you within 2 business days. A corrected invoice keeps its original payment cycle as long as it arrives before the 10th.
- Rates are reviewed once a year, in March, together with the contract renewal.

## Overlap with Buenos Aires

- Be online at least 4 hours a day, Monday to Friday, inside the 10:00–18:00 window in Buenos Aires time (ART, UTC−3).
- Those 4 hours must include your team's daily stand-up and any client meeting scheduled inside that window.
- Post your weekly schedule in your team's Slack channel every Monday morning.
- If you live more than 5 hours away from Buenos Aires time, agree on a written schedule with your lead before your start date.

## Equipment

Contractors work with their own computer, phone and internet connection, and there is no equipment allowance for contractors. Acme only lends hardware when a client project needs a specific device (for example, a test phone), and it goes back to the Palermo office when the engagement ends. Acme does pay for the software licenses you need for client work, which the account lead requests for you.

Your computer must meet our security baseline: full-disk encryption turned on, automatic screen lock and an operating system that still receives security updates. IT and Security may ask you to confirm this once a year.

## Public holidays and time off

- You may take the national public holidays of your country of residence. Let your lead know at least 5 business days in advance.
- Argentine public holidays are not working days for most of the team: don't expect replies or schedule internal meetings on those dates.
- You can take up to 20 business days of unpaid time off per year without affecting your contract. Give 15 calendar days' notice for any absence of 3 days or more.
- Holidays and days off are not invoiced.

## Availability and response times

- Slack messages during your overlap window: reply within 2 business hours.
- Client emails: reply within 1 business day, copying the account lead.
- Update your Slack status and calendar whenever you are away. For absences longer than 2 business days, also tell the account lead of every client you work on.
- Contractors are not part of the weekend on-call rotation unless their contract says so. When they are, each on-call weekend is invoiced as a flat fee of USD 150.
- Missing your overlap window twice in the same month without notice leads to a review conversation with your lead.
